orders.dependency_condition: Absorbs the capability layer first (order 50), so 47 projects the semantic trio over that mechanism instead of inventing a second vocabulary; the capability branch touched the same three Server files, so the two must not be written concurrently.
orders.note: The upper layer states requirements, the resolved sandbox provider translates them. Today the channels import the bwrap composer directly (sidecar.py:316, local_channel.py:25), bootstrap hard-imports WslConnector (runtime.py:139) and the layout grammar (runtime.py:727/739/784), the coordinator is never called on the product path, the sandbox never declares isolation.wrap@1 while preflight treats an undeclared capability as passing, and legacy_codex.py is dead code that would re-fuse the layers if revived. This order consumes the existing protocol (MountPlan -> wrap -> IsolatedProcessSpec), unifies the two capability vocabularies and makes an undeclared capability a refusal, moves the layout grammar into the contracts layer, registers the wsl host provider, adds a sandbox conformance gate whose counter-example must fail, and keeps behaviour byte-identical (the substitution gate and the four family gates stay green). Deployment document format does not change. Real model calls: zero. Runs after order 50, which absorbs the capability layer from feature/capability-entry-v1 by content.

orders.note: Native Windows placement: Server on Windows, harness on Windows, AppContainer as the sandbox (capability based, access granted by ACL, no virtualisation so the home stays a real directory), a Job Object for the tree and its lifetime, and no Worker at all because the Server already runs on that machine and reads the directory directly for the audit. Materialisation has no bind mount to lean on, so config goes to a per-execution directory pointed at by environment variables (or into the home with an ACL granting read only, when a harness insists on a fixed filename), credentials go into the child's environment block, and the tmpfs masks become 'do not write plus delete', never recorded as masked. Read isolation is the linchpin: the official wording is that read-only access is less restricted, so it must be measured, and if reads are not denied the capability is declared false and the platform is reported as weaker than Linux. Wasted: Windows Sandbox (VM shape, mapped folders are a redirected filesystem), Windows containers, Sandboxie, minifilters, and remapping (junctions or a per-process DOS device) except when a harness hardcodes a path.

orders.note: Absorbs by content what feature/capability-entry-v1 (baseline 897a833, HEAD 1c74d15) built for capability entry: the agent_box.extensions.capability package (ids, requirements, match, selection, documents, errors), the sandbox-side declarations.py with per-execution declaration documents, and roughly 2000 lines of tests - without merging that branch, its history, its own dispatch snapshot under dispatch/agentbox-system/, or its CAP-02..05 queue. The design commitments worth keeping verbatim: the declarable set must be a subset of the actually enforceable set (a target outside the plugin's own path grammar is a typed refusal, not a smaller claim), every declaration carries a file-symbol evidence anchor bound to the execution environment and time, an honest 'unavailable' state exists (the remote argv never emits --unshare-net), declaration providers must appear in an explicit approval map because installed-or-loaded is not authorization, and grants come from the deployment document plus module constants rather than from the declaration document itself. It also converges a real over-claim found while reading: _CAPS declares network.none@1 supported for the whole provider while the sidecar compiler never emits --unshare-net. Zero real model calls; wire untouched.

orders.note: Real usage and context numbers, end to end, reported only when the harness actually reports them. Nothing in the chain carries usage today: the sidecar bridge and the opencode driver have zero usage handling, the Server's _forward() knows only message chunks, permission requests and exits, and the wire has no usage field at all - and the vendored ACP SDK definition has no usage or contextWindow, so the ACP families cannot supply it at the protocol level and need another source, which stage A must establish per family. The denominator (context window) is a separate source from the numerator and must be found per family, otherwise the percentage stays unknown. The fact added to the envelope is neutral (no brand names, no guessed fields), the Server records it in the turn ledger and a session-level latest value, and the wire change is the minimum that works with a two-repository relock. Estimation is forbidden: a family that does not report shows unknown, and the frontend container from P08 consumes only what arrives.

orders.note: The process facts a ZCode/Codex-style transcript needs already exist upstream and are being dropped: the ACP schema's sessionUpdate vocabulary is agent_message_chunk, agent_thought_chunk, tool_call, tool_call_update, plan_update, plan_removed and current_mode_update, while the bridge and the Server's _forward() know only agent_message_chunk. This order maps thoughts, the tool lifecycle, plans and mode changes into neutral events, derives durations from the existing event timestamps instead of adding estimated fields, and shares ONE wire relock with order 51 (usage) to avoid two contract churns. Tool arguments and outputs are trimmed and scanned before they enter the ledger. No fake progress: a family that emits nothing shows nothing.
